records.context: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. An extracted image region the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the extracted image regions worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work list ordered so the informative extracted image regions come first.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#1
records.source: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. A crop the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the crops worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work queue ordered so the informative crops come first.
records.translation: 주석 작업은 모든 스크리닝의 병목입니다. 모델이 이미 0.999로 판정한 추출된 이미지 영역은 사람이 라벨을 달아도 모델에 아무것도 가르쳐 주지 않습니다. 사람의 오후 시간을 쓸 가치가 있는 추출된 이미지 영역은 결정 경계에 놓인 것들입니다. 이 모듈은 이미 점수가 매겨진 ``measurements.db`` 를 정보량이 많은 추출된 이미지 영역이 먼저 오도록 정렬된 작업 목록으로 바꿉니다.

records.context: **Already-annotated extracted image regions never enter the annotation work list.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the extracted image region has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and an annotation work list that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.label: spacr.active_learning#6
records.source: **Already-annotated crops never enter the queue.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the crop has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and a queue that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.translation: **이미 주석이 달린 추출된 이미지 영역은 주석 작업 목록에 절대 들어가지 않습니다.** 주석 열의 ``NULL`` 은 판정 보류 표시로, 해당 추출된 이미지 영역을 아직 아무도 보지 않았다는 뜻입니다. ``0`` 은 실제 클래스이며, 이를 다시 내놓는 작업 목록은 이 모듈이 아끼려고 존재하는 바로 그 자원을 낭비합니다. 둘은 ``IS NULL`` 로 구별하며, 거짓 값 여부로는 절대 구별하지 않습니다. ( :mod:`spacr.agreement` 와 같은 규칙입니다.)

records.context: ``margin`` and ``least_confidence`` are the same ranking on two classes. For C = 2, ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: a linear transform, so identical order and identical ties. They are not two independent choices on a binary screen — they differ only from three classes up, where ``margin`` looks at the top *two* classes while ``least_confidence`` looks only at the top one and ``entropy`` looks at the whole distribution.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#8
records.source: ``margin`` and ``least_confidence`` are the same ranking on two classes. For C = 2, ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: a linear transform, so identical order and identical ties. They are not two independent choices on a binary screen — they differ only from three classes up, where ``margin`` looks at the top *two* classes while ``least_confidence`` looks only at the top one and ``entropy`` looks at the whole distribution.
records.translation: ``margin`` 과 ``least_confidence`` 는 두 클래스에서 동일한 순위를 냅니다. C = 2 일 때 ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)`` : 선형 변환이므로 순서도 동일하고 동점도 동일합니다. 이진 스크리닝에서 이 둘은 서로 독립적인 두 선택지가 아닙니다 — 클래스가 세 개 이상일 때만 달라지며, 이때 ``margin`` 은 상위 *두* 클래스를 보고, ``least_confidence`` 는 최상위 하나만 보며, ``entropy`` 는 전체 분포를 봅니다.

records.context: ``n`` **is the number of rows the matrix actually contains**, and the supports sum to it. A row whose true class the head has no column for is counted as an error rather than dropped: the matrix grows to hold it, and the missing column stays empty because the head can never predict that class. Reporting ``n`` over one population and ``accuracy`` over another is the one thing a model card must not do — a three-class held-out set scored by a binary head used to report a perfect score on a set the model got two of three right, and the ``accuracy == trace / total`` invariant still checked out because the row was missing from both sides of it.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.holdout_report#3
records.source: ``n`` **is the number of rows the matrix actually contains**, and the supports sum to it. A row whose true class the head has no column for is counted as an error rather than dropped: the matrix grows to hold it, and the missing column stays empty because the head can never predict that class. Reporting ``n`` over one population and ``accuracy`` over another is the one thing a model card must not do — a three-class held-out set scored by a binary head used to report a perfect score on a set the model got two of three right, and the ``accuracy == trace / total`` invariant still checked out because the row was missing from both sides of it.
records.translation: ``n`` **은 행렬에 실제로 들어 있는 행의 수** 이며, 지지도의 합이 이 값과 같습니다. 참 클래스에 해당하는 열이 헤드에 없는 행은 버려지는 대신 오류로 계산됩니다: 행렬은 그 행을 담기 위해 커지고, 헤드가 그 클래스를 절대 예측할 수 없으므로 빠진 열은 비어 있게 됩니다. ``n`` 은 한 모집단에 대해, ``accuracy`` 는 다른 모집단에 대해 보고하는 것은 모델 카드가 절대 해서는 안 되는 일입니다 — 이전에는 이진 헤드가 점수를 매긴 3-클래스 홀드아웃 세트가, 모델이 세 개 중 두 개만 맞힌 세트에서 만점을 보고했고, ``accuracy == trace / total`` 불변식은 그 행이 양쪽 모두에서 빠져 있었기 때문에 여전히 성립했습니다.

records.context: The rule, in one line: look back over whole rounds until at least ``label_window`` new labels have accumulated, and compare held-out accuracy at the two ends. If it moved by less than ``min_gain``, stop.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#1
records.source: The rule, in one line: look back over whole rounds until at least ``label_window`` new labels have accumulated, and compare held-out accuracy at the two ends. If it moved by less than ``min_gain``, stop.
records.translation: 규칙을 한 줄로: 새 라벨이 최소 ``label_window`` 개 쌓일 때까지 전체 라운드를 거슬러 살펴보고, 양 끝에서 홀드아웃 정확도를 비교합니다. 변화가 ``min_gain`` 보다 작으면 멈춥니다.

records.context: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#4
records.source: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.translation: **라운드를 *거슬러* 살펴보며, 마지막 라운드 *하나* 만 보지 않습니다.** 우연히 변화 없이 끝난 라운드 하나는 잡음일 뿐입니다. 질문은 마지막 50개의 라벨이 — 어떻게 나뉘었든 — 무언가를 얻어 냈느냐입니다.

records.context: ``NAN_DROP_FEATURES`` drop any feature column containing a NaN. Cheap and safe; on a real database it often removes every ``pathogen_*`` column, which is the honest consequence of asking for a complete matrix. ``NAN_DROP_OBJECTS`` drop any object row containing a NaN. Usually removes almost everything, for the same reason; offered because on a single-object-type export it is often exactly right. ``NAN_ZERO`` / ``NAN_MEAN`` impute. Both write a ``layers['missing']`` boolean mask of the same shape by default, because an imputed matrix that cannot be told from a measured one is a trap, and 1 byte per cell against 4 is a fair price.
records.label: spacr.anndata_export#15
records.source: ``NAN_DROP_FEATURES`` drop any feature column containing a NaN. Cheap and safe; on a real database it often removes every ``pathogen_*`` column, which is the honest consequence of asking for a complete matrix. ``NAN_DROP_OBJECTS`` drop any object row containing a NaN. Usually removes almost everything, for the same reason; offered because on a single-object-type export it is often exactly right. ``NAN_ZERO`` / ``NAN_MEAN`` impute. Both write a ``layers['missing']`` boolean mask of the same shape by default, because an imputed matrix that cannot be told from a measured one is a trap, and 1 byte per cell against 4 is a fair price.
records.translation: ``NAN_DROP_FEATURES`` NaN 을 포함하는 특징 열을 모두 제거합니다. 저렴하고 안전하지만, 실제 데이터베이스에서는 흔히 ``pathogen_*`` 열이 전부 제거되는데, 이는 완전한 행렬을 요구한 데 따른 정직한 결과입니다. ``NAN_DROP_OBJECTS`` NaN 을 포함하는 객체 행을 모두 제거합니다. 같은 이유로 대개 거의 모든 것이 제거되지만, 단일 객체 유형 내보내기에서는 정확히 맞는 경우가 많아 제공됩니다. ``NAN_ZERO`` / ``NAN_MEAN`` 값을 대치합니다. 둘 다 기본적으로 같은 형태의 불리언 마스크 ``layers['missing']`` 를 기록합니다. 측정값과 구별할 수 없는 대치된 행렬은 함정이며, 셀당 4바이트에 대해 1바이트는 합당한 비용이기 때문입니다.

records.context: **Infinities are treated as missing under every policy.** spaCR produces +/-inf from ratio features (a denominator of zero), and an inf survives ``dropna`` while destroying any scaling, PCA or distance computed from it. They are converted to NaN before the policy runs and counted separately in ``uns['spacr']['nan']['n_infinite']`` so the substitution is never silent.
records.label: spacr.anndata_export#16
records.source: **Infinities are treated as missing under every policy.** spaCR produces +/-inf from ratio features (a denominator of zero), and an inf survives ``dropna`` while destroying any scaling, PCA or distance computed from it. They are converted to NaN before the policy runs and counted separately in ``uns['spacr']['nan']['n_infinite']`` so the substitution is never silent.
records.translation: **무한대 값은 모든 정책에서 결측으로 취급됩니다.** spaCR 은 비율 특징(분모가 0인 경우)에서 +/-inf 를 만들어 내며, inf 는 ``dropna`` 를 통과해 살아남는 동시에 그로부터 계산되는 모든 스케일링, PCA, 거리를 망가뜨립니다. 따라서 정책이 실행되기 전에 NaN 으로 변환되고 ``uns['spacr']['nan']['n_infinite']`` 에 따로 집계되므로, 이 치환은 결코 조용히 일어나지 않습니다.

records.context: :func:`spacr.io._read_and_join_tables` takes six named columns off ``png_list`` -- the object id, ``png_path`` and the four microscope field of view structured-data names -- and drops the rest. records.context: AnnData stores NaN happily. Most of what people reach for next does not: ``sc.pp.scale``, ``sc.pp.pca``, ``sc.pp.neighbors`` and essentially all of scvi-tools either propagate NaN across the whole matrix or raise. So a silent default matters, and there are only two honest candidates: keep the NaN and say so loudly, or impute and say so loudly. Quietly filling with zero is not one of them -- in spaCR a NaN is usually *meaningful*: a ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it, a Zernike column is NaN when mahotas was not installed, and a correlation column is NaN when one channel was flat. Zero-filling the first turns "no pathogen" into "a pathogen of zero size" and puts it into the same distribution as a measured one.

records.translation: AnnData 는 NaN 을 문제없이 저장합니다. 그다음에 사람들이 손을 뻗는 대부분의 도구는 그렇지 않습니다: ``sc.pp.scale``, ``sc.pp.pca``, ``sc.pp.neighbors`` 그리고 사실상 scvi-tools 전체가 NaN 을 행렬 전체로 전파하거나 예외를 발생시킵니다. 그래서 조용한 기본값이 중요하며, 정직한 후보는 두 가지뿐입니다: NaN 을 유지하고 그 사실을 분명히 알리거나, 값을 대치하고 그 사실을 분명히 알리는 것. 조용히 0으로 채우는 것은 그중 하나가 아닙니다 -- spaCR 에서 NaN 은 대개 *의미가 있습니다*: ``pathogen_*`` 열은 병원체가 없는 세포에서 NaN 이고, Zernike 열은 mahotas 가 설치되지 않았을 때 NaN 이며, 상관 열은 한 채널이 평탄했을 때 NaN 입니다. 첫 번째를 0으로 채우면 "no pathogen"(병원체 없음)이 "크기가 0인 병원체"로 바뀌어 측정된 것과 같은 분포에 들어갑니다.

This mirrors :func:`spacr.zstack.resolve_anisotropy`, which raises rather than defaulting to 1.0 because "isotropic" is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value. records.context: **The pyramid.** ``levels=1`` writes level 0 alone; more builds each level by halving the two fastest-varying space axes of the one above with a 2x **block mean** (``downsample="mean"``) or by **striding** (``downsample="stride"``). Neither is a Gaussian pyramid — there is no pre-filter beyond the box — and the block mean is the default because striding aliases: a one-pixel-wide bright structure survives or vanishes with the parity of its coordinate, so the same object appears and disappears as a user zooms. **Label and mask arrays must use** ``downsample="stride"``: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, which is a different object, and averaging a boolean mask invents half-membership. Levels shrink by ``ceil(n / 2)``, so nothing is cropped off an odd edge.

records.context: Returning exactly ``False`` stops the sweep and returns the rows completed so far; anything else (including ``None``) continues.  This exists for one reason: a sweep is minutes long and a GUI has to be able to show where it is and to stop it without killing the independent execution path.  Between points is the only safe granularity — one fit is atomic — so a cancel is honoured after the fit in flight, not during it.  The callback executes on the calling independent execution path, inline; it must not block, and a callback that raises aborts the sweep rather than being swallowed, because a broken progress reporter is a bug in the caller and hiding it would leave the sweep executing with nothing watching it.

records.source: Returning exactly ``False`` stops the sweep and returns the rows completed so far; anything else (including ``None``) continues. records.context: A pooled Toxoplasma CRISPR screening experiment has three noisy layers stacked on top of each other — which genotypes landed in which well, how many of a well's cells the microscope saw and how well the machine-learning classification model called them, and how many reads each genotype got out of the amplicon pool. The question a screener has to answer *before* spending the microscope time is "with this library, this many microplate sample positions, this many cells per well and a machine-learning classification model at 0.80/0.12, would I actually find a hit?". That is a statistical detection sensitivity analysis, and it is only answerable by simulation because no layer is analytically tractable once the other two are stacked on it.

records.context: ``clear RAM`` Drops spaCR's own caches: the merged-microscope field of view LRU (:func:`spacr.crops.clear_field_cache` — by far the largest, whole image stacks), the file-format and DB-format caches, the zoomed-animation cache, the icon and preview ``lru_cache``\ s, the filter-kind cache, every live :class:`~spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails` thumbnail LRU, and Qt's own ``QPixmapCache``. A process with no live Qt application also runs ``gc.collect()``. The GUI deliberately does not: walking a heap of live Qt wrappers can enter already-retired C++ objects and crash the process. It cannot return memory the allocator has decided to keep, and it says so when the measured RSS does not move.

records.translation: ``clear RAM`` spaCR 자체의 캐시를 비웁니다: 병합된 현미경 필드 LRU( :func:`spacr.crops.clear_field_cache` — 단연 가장 큰 것으로, 이미지 스택 전체), 파일 형식 및 DB 형식 캐시, 확대 애니메이션 캐시, 아이콘과 미리보기 ``lru_cache``\ s, 필터 종류 캐시, 활성 상태인 모든 :class:`~spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails` 썸네일 LRU, 그리고 Qt 자체의 ``QPixmapCache``. 실행 중인 Qt 애플리케이션이 없는 프로세스는 ``gc.collect()`` 도 실행합니다. records.context: 1. ``set_default_settings_preprocess_generate_masks`` defaults it to the **string** ``'cell'``, and ``measure.py`` tests it with ``"organelle" in settings['summarize_organelles_by']`` — a *substring* test when the value is a str. Running this demo with ``summarize_organelles_by='cell'`` gives ``cell_organelle_summary`` (16 rows/field) and still no ``organelle`` table. Only a value containing ``'organelle'`` writes the per-organelle table (``['cell', 'organelle']`` → organelle 64 rows/field, verified). 2. The tooltip and ``spacr.gui_utils`` both describe it as a list, and ``spacr.external_masks`` builds one; only the type table disagrees.

records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_``, and that is load-bearing. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. The version this replaces asked for ``max(rowid)`` and got two things wrong at once on every real measurements database: it scanned the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table — precisely the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method exists to avoid), and then ``int('r16')`` raised ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and so escaped the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` all carry a comment about this shadowing; this method had not got the memo.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.

records.context: spaCR runs concentration series and has, until this module, had no curve fitter at all: a screener with eight doses and three replicates exports a CSV and opens Prism. The point of writing one is not that "it fits" — every optimiser fits — but that **the answer is often "you cannot tell from this experiment", and no fitter in common use says so.** ``curve_fit`` will return four numbers and a covariance matrix for a dilution series that never reached a plateau, for a bell-shaped cytotoxicity curve, and for eight points of pure noise. All three come back looking like an EC50 with a confidence interval.

records.context: 1. **The curve is incomplete** — one plateau was never reached, or the midpoint sits outside the tested range. Then the EC50 is an extrapolation. :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50` is ``None`` in that case and the number lives in :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_unconstrained`, under a name that cannot be mistaken for a result; :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_bounded` is ``False`` and :meth:`DoseResponseResult.bound_statement` gives the one-sided fact the experiment does support ("EC50 > 30 µM, the highest concentration tested"). Three independent detectors have to agree it is fine before a number is released: the fitted midpoint inside the tested dose range, the observed responses bracketing the fitted half-maximum, and neither fitted plateau more than :data:`PLATEAU_SLACK` of the observed response span outside the observed responses. 2. **The data is not monotone.** A bell shape — the classic being cytotoxicity killing the signal at the top dose — is not a 4PL, and a 4PL fitted to it returns a confident EC50 for a curve of the wrong shape. Detected from the concentration-ordered per-dose medians and **refused**, with the concentrations where it turns named in the message. See :func:`monotonicity`. 3. **There is not enough experiment.** Four parameters need at least four distinct concentrations (:data:`MIN_DOSES`) and, to say anything about uncertainty, more observations than parameters (:data:`MIN_OBSERVATIONS`). A constant response has no curve in it. A **zero concentration is not an error** — a vehicle control is normal and belongs in the file — so it is excluded from the fit deliberately, counted, and reported as a reference response, never fed to ``log10``. A *negative* concentration has no such reading and is refused.

records.context: The obvious thing to write here is ``|x - mean| / sd > 3``, and it is the one thing this module refuses to do. spaCR object measurements are skewed and heavy-tailed by construction: ``cell_area`` is a positive quantity with a long right tail, ``pathogen_area`` is zero-inflated, an intensity ratio has a denominator that can approach zero. The mean and the SD of such a column are themselves dragged by the very objects they are supposed to find — one debris particle measured at 40× the median area moves the mean, inflates the SD, and so raises the threshold that was meant to catch it. The failure is silent and it gets worse the worse the contamination is: this is the *masking* effect, and it is the reason robust statistics exist.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#2

The mean and the SD of such a column are themselves dragged by the very objects they are supposed to find — one debris particle measured at 40× the median area moves the mean, inflates the SD, and so raises the threshold that was meant to catch it. The failure is silent and it gets worse the worse the contamination is: this is the *masking* effect, and it is the reason robust statistics exist.
records.translation: 여기서 가장 먼저 떠오르는 방식은 ``|x - mean| / sd > 3`` 이지만, 이 모듈이 거부하는 단 한 가지가 바로 그것입니다. spaCR 의 객체 측정값은 원래부터 치우쳐 있고 꼬리가 두껍습니다: ``cell_area`` 는 오른쪽 꼬리가 긴 양수 값이고, ``pathogen_area`` 는 0 이 과도하게 많으며, 강도 비율은 분모가 0 에 가까워질 수 있습니다. 이런 열의 평균과 SD 는 그것들이 찾아내야 할 바로 그 객체들에 의해 끌려갑니다 — 중앙값 면적의 40× 로 측정된 파편 입자 하나가 평균을 움직이고 SD 를 부풀려, 결국 그것을 잡아내야 할 임계값을 높여 버립니다. 이 실패는 조용히 일어나며 오염이 심할수록 더 나빠집니다: 이것이 *마스킹* 효과이며, 강건 통계가 존재하는 이유입니다.

records.context: **MCD is the multivariate generalisation of the median and the MAD.** The MCD centre is a multivariate median (the mean of the h-subset of minimum covariance determinant) and the MCD scatter is its spread. So all three methods offered here are the same idea at one, one, and p dimensions, and a user who understands the MAD already understands this.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#22

records.context: **The cost, stated.** MCD needs ``n > p`` to have a covariance at all, and it is unstable until roughly ``n >= 2p`` (:data:`MCD_MIN_OBJECTS_PER_FEATURE` * p): the estimate is fitted on a *subset* of about ``n/2`` rows, so ``n = 2p`` already means the subset is only barely larger than the dimension. Its breakdown point is set by ``support_fraction``: the sklearn default of ``(n + p + 1) / 2n`` gives the maximum ~50%, and raising it trades robustness for efficiency. Too few objects for the number of features is **refused with a message that names the way out**: run a PCA first (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.pca`) and flag on the first few components, which are fewer, uncorrelated, and carry the same information.

records.translation: **객체 세 개로는 웰에 점수를 매기지 않습니다.** :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_WELL_OBJECTS` 개 미만의 객체에서는 중앙값의 잡음이 너무 커서 웰 간 비교가 의미를 가질 수 없으므로, 그 웰은 ``well_scored = False`` 로 웰 프레임에 나타나며 객체가 몇 개였는지 알려 주는 이유가 함께 표시됩니다. 이런 웰은 **절대 조용히 빠지지도, 조용히 점수가 매겨지지도 않습니다** — 아무 말 없이 제외된 n 이 작은 웰이야말로 빈 웰이 눈에 띄지 않는 한 행으로 묻히는 방식이기 때문입니다.

records.context: **MAD == 0 is handled, not divided by.** When more than half the objects share one value — a zero-inflated ``pathogen_area``, an integer count, a saturated intensity — the MAD is exactly zero. Naively, every value that differs at all then scores infinity and *the entire tail is flagged*, which is the opposite of robust. So :func:`robust_scale` falls back to the **mean absolute deviation from the median**, scaled by :data:`MEAN_AD_TO_SIGMA` = ``sqrt(pi/2)`` = 1.2533 (for a Gaussian ``E|X - mu| = sigma * sqrt(2/pi)``), and says so in :attr:`OutlierResult.notes` and in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#8

So :func:`robust_scale` falls back to the **mean absolute deviation from the median**, scaled by :data:`MEAN_AD_TO_SIGMA` = ``sqrt(pi/2)`` = 1.2533 (for a Gaussian ``E|X - mu| = sigma * sqrt(2/pi)``), and says so in :attr:`OutlierResult.notes` and in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`.
records.translation: **MAD == 0 은 나누는 값으로 쓰지 않고 따로 처리합니다.** 객체의 절반 이상이 같은 값을 가질 때 — 0 이 과도하게 많은 ``pathogen_area``, 정수 개수, 포화된 강도 — MAD 는 정확히 0 입니다. 순진하게 처리하면 조금이라도 다른 모든 값이 무한대 점수를 받아 *꼬리 전체가 표시* 되는데, 이는 강건함과 정반대입니다. 그래서 :func:`robust_scale` 은 **중앙값으로부터의 평균 절대 편차** 로 대체하고 :data:`MEAN_AD_TO_SIGMA` = ``sqrt(pi/2)`` = 1.2533 으로 척도를 맞추며(가우시안에서는 ``E|X - mu| = sigma * sqrt(2/pi)``), 이 사실을 :attr:`OutlierResult.notes` 와 :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats` 에 밝힙니다.

records.context: The alternative considered and not taken is the Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), which is the statistically better answer: it has a 50% breakdown point, needs no symmetry assumption, and does not collapse on tied data. It is not used because the naive form is O(n^2) — unusable on the 10^5–10^6 object rows spaCR routinely produces — and the O(n log n) algorithm is a page of intricate code to maintain for a path that is only ever reached when the MAD has *already* collapsed. The mean absolute deviation has a 0% breakdown point and that is stated plainly rather than glossed: it is a stopgap that keeps a degenerate column from flagging its whole tail, not a robust estimator. If the fallback fires, the honest reading is that the column is not continuous enough for this test.

records.translation: 고려했지만 채택하지 않은 대안은 Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``) 으로, 통계적으로는 더 나은 답입니다: 붕괴점이 50% 이고, 대칭 가정이 필요 없으며, 동률이 많은 데이터에서도 무너지지 않습니다. 그래도 쓰지 않는 이유는 단순한 형태가 O(n^2) 이어서 spaCR 이 일상적으로 만들어 내는 10^5–10^6 개의 객체 행에서는 사용할 수 없고, O(n log n) 알고리즘은 MAD 가 *이미* 무너졌을 때만 도달하는 경로를 위해 유지해야 하는 한 페이지 분량의 복잡한 코드이기 때문입니다. 평균 절대 편차는 붕괴점이 0% 이며, 이 사실은 얼버무리지 않고 분명히 밝힙니다: 그것은 강건 추정량이 아니라, 퇴화된 열이 꼬리 전체를 표시하지 못하게 막는 임시방편입니다. 이 대체 경로가 작동했다면, 정직한 해석은 그 열이 이 검정을 적용할 만큼 연속적이지 않다는 것입니다.

records.context: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for an honest NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.

records.translation: **값이 전혀 없는 열이 돌아올 때의 타입은** ``object`` 입니다. 이것은 흔한 경우이며 데이터 문제가 아닙니다: ``pandas.read_sql`` 은 받은 행으로 프레임을 만들기 때문에, 모든 행에서 ``NULL`` 인 열은 ``None`` 으로 된 열로 도착하고 pandas 는 그 타입을 ``object`` 로 정합니다 -- SQLite 가 그 열을 ``REAL`` 로 선언했더라도 말입니다. spaCR 은 정직한 NaN 에 대해 ``NULL`` 을 기록하며, 어떤 측정값은 데이터베이스 전체에서 정당하게 NaN 입니다: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` 는 균일한 객체마다 NaN 이고, ``mode_intensity`` 는 ``measure._extended_regionprops_table`` 에 SciPy 호환 계층이 들어가기 전에 기록된 모든 데이터베이스에서 모든 객체에 대해 NaN 이었습니다. 이런 열은 ``float64`` NaN 으로 변환되며, 이는 원래부터 그 열이 뜻하던 바입니다. 잃는 것이 없으므로 경고도 하지 않습니다 -- 그리고 호출자 자신의 전체-NaN 필터가 그 열을 제거하고 그 사실을 알립니다.

records.translation: ``spacr/`` 전체를 감사한 결과 테이블 형식의 읽기와 쓰기 248 곳 -- ``pd.read_csv``, ``pd.read_sql*``, ``.to_csv``, ``.to_sql`` -- 을 찾았는데, 그중 열 이름을 조금이라도 정규화한 호출 지점은 **열세** 곳뿐이었습니다. 깔때기는 없었습니다; 문이 248 개 있었고, 프레임이 어떤 철자의 키를 갖게 되는지는 어느 문을 통해 들어왔느냐에 달려 있었습니다.
